thread:
mira: Quick kickoff 1: fingerprint mapping constraints for v1->v2 migration. We need a stable mapping strategy that preserves auditability and prevents billing flips.

jon: Agree. core requirements: reversible mapping (for audits), compact storage, and low-latency lookups during backfill.

sam: Operational constraints: backfills must not change past invoices. If mapping changes produced different granularity, we need compensating entries not rewrites.

teja: Proposal: emit both fingerprints during migration window: fp_old and fp_new. Ledger stores primary_fp = fp_new but keeps fp_old in mapping table indexed by raw_archive_key. Backfills and reconciler use raw_archive_key to reconcile.

mira: That matches my thoughts. Two immediate questions: storage size (mapping table cardinality) and lookup hotness for heavy tenants.

alex: For storage, compact the mapping table by TTL (e.g., 90 days) plus sampling for long-tail. For heavy tenants we may keep mappings longer behind per-tenant policy. Legal/compliance must sign off on retention.

jon: Lookup perf: avoid N+1 lookups at ingest. Design pattern: during backfill, we stream raw_archive_keys with events to a join worker that fetches mapping table in batch (windowed joins). That keeps ingestion path clean.

sam: What about realtime reconciliation during dual-write? We might get duplicate credit deltas if both v1 and v2 become visible to ledger. We need deterministic idempotency keys.

teja: Idempotency key suggestion: sha256(tenant_id + request_id + canonical_fp). For v1 events without request_id, fallback to sha256(raw_archive_key). Ledger enforces idempotency and emits de-dup events to metrics.

billing-bot: billing: note: invoices must be stable. Any compensating adjustments must be surfaced as "metering-correction" line items with clear provenance.

mira: Good point. Backfill plan must publish compensation policy and threshold for auto-adjust vs manual approval. Propose auto-adjust if delta < 0.1% of monthly tokens; else require manual review.

jon: Edge-case: fp function change where many old events collapse into fewer new fingerprints or vice versa. That can create large token diffs. For collapse case (many->one) backfill should dedupe using mapping table and ledger should aggregate to the canonical_fp without reassigning to different tenant. For expansion (one->many) we need to record original counts per raw event to split appropriately.

sam: For expansion: store original_token_count in mapping row so replay knows how to allocate. Avoid trying to infer tokens from model outputs later.

teja: Schema sketch for mapping table (pseudo-cols): [raw_archive_key, fp_old, fp_new, original_token_count, created_ts, tenant_id, migration_tag]. Keep columns minimal strings/numbers, partition by tenant_id+date.

mira: Backfill throttling: default 500 events/sec per tenant, with burst tokens and a global cluster budget. Implement circuit-breaker: if reconciliation drift > 0.5% in 1h, pause backfill for that tenant and notify support.

alex: Also add a "dry-run" backfill mode that writes metrics and produces proposed ledger deltas to a staging ledger. Customers can opt-in to run dry-run before real backfill. That helps avoid surprise billing.

jon: For visibility: expose migration progress per-tenant: total_raw_events, processed_events, estimated_time_remaining, current_backfill_rate, current_drift. API must be paginated for large runs.

sam: Monitoring: emit reconciliation histograms by tenant, hourly drift gauges, duplicate-credit counters, and a backfill-health summary. Alert thresholds: duplicate credits > 0.2% (1h) or drift > 0.3% (24h).

teja: Security/PII: raw_archive_key may point to S3 objects containing user identifiers. Ensure backfill workers run in private VPC and access keys rotated. Also encrypt mapping table at rest.

mira: Owner assignments: ingest team implements dual-write shim & raw_archive_key emission; infra builds mapping table storage and batch join; ledger team implements idempotency semantics and compaction; support builds progress API + dry-run UI; billing drafts compensation policy.

alex: Timeline proposal: 1) prototype shim + mapping table (2 weeks), 2) perf canary (1 week), 3) partner migrations + dry-runs (4 weeks), 4) full migration rollout (120-day opt-in).

jon: Action items: I'll author a short interface contract for mapping rows and idempotency key generation. mira: please capture the compensation policy and dry-run requirements. sam: kick off metrics/alerts tickets. teja: sketch mapping table DDL.

mira: Will publish RFC follow-up with all artifacts and schedule a 30-min sync Friday to confirm owners.

alex: Thanks. TL;DR: keep ingestion light, store mapping with raw keys, batch join for backfill, idempotency in ledger, dry-run + compensation policy to protect invoices. Closing thread once doc is live.
